questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Empress of India Act:
1. The original name of the Act was the Royal Titles Act, 1877.
2. It officially recognized Queen Victoria as the Empress of India.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is incorrect: The correct original name is the Royal Titles Act, 1876, not 1877.
  • Statement 2 is correct: It officially recognized Queen Victoria as the Empress of India.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts regard trade unions as well as individual workmen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Industrial Disputes Act.
The Industrial Disputes Act of 1947 regards trade unions as well as individual workmen. The Rowlatt Act (1919) authorized arrest without trial for 2 years. Indian Council Acts (1861, 1892, 1909) and Charter Acts (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853) dealt with other matters.

questions.question: Which Act passed by British Government of India abolished the Council of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Government of India Act of 1935.
The Government of India Act 1935 had the following key features:
  • Abolition of provincial dyarchy and introduction of dyarchy at the centre
  • Abolition of the Indian Council and introduction of an advisory body in its place
  • Provision for an All India Federation with British India territories and princely states

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sharda Act of 1929:
1. The Sharda Act fixed the marriageable age for girls at 14 years and boys at 18 years.
2. The Act was sponsored by Harbilas Sarda.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both statements are True.
The Sharda Act fixed the marriageable age for girls at 14 years and 18 years for boys. It was sponsored by Harbilas Sarda. Other important acts: Pitt's India Act (1784), Rowlatt Act (1919), Vernacular Press Act (1878).

questions.question: In which year through the Indian Official Secrets Act was freedom of press curbed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1904.
The Indian Official Secrets Act was enacted in 1904 during the time of Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905, and it curbed the freedom of the press. Later this act was replaced by the Official Secrets Act of 1923.

questions.question: In 1877, which of the following viceroys organized a durbar to acknowledge Queen Victoria as the Empress of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Lytton.
Lord Lytton organized a Durbar in 1877 to acknowledge Queen Victoria as the Empress of India. This was the culmination of the transfer of control of British India from the East India Company to the British Crown.

questions.question: The capital of the British Indian Empire was transferred from Calcutta to Delhi in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1911.
The British government believed that ruling India from Delhi was easier and more convenient than from Calcutta. Therefore, Delhi was officially announced as the capital of the British Raj by Emperor George V on December 12, 1911.

questions.question: By which British statute were Indian representatives, for the first time, allocated seats for election in Indian Legislative Councils?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Indian Councils Act, 1892.
The Indian Councils Act of 1892 made a limited and indirect provision for the use of election in filling up some of the non-official seats both in the Central and provincial legislative councils. This was the first time Indian representatives were allocated seats through an electoral process.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. General Dyer imposed Martial Law in India in 1920, under which public gatherings of more than two people were prohibited.
2. The office of the first Accountant General in India was established in 1858, the same year the British Crown took over administration from the East India Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is incorrect: General Dyer imposed Martial Law in 1919 (not 1920), in response to the Rowlatt Act protests, which culminated in the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
  • Statement 2 is correct: The office of the first Accountant General in India was established in 1858, the same year the British Crown took over administration from the East India Company.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905 by Lord Curzon.
2. The Surat Split of the Indian National Congress took place in 1909 between the Moderates and Extremists.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905 by Lord Curzon.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Surat Split took place in 1907, not 1909, between the Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale) and the Extremists (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Rakhi-tying movement:
1. In 1905, Rabindranath Tagore encouraged Hindus and Muslims to tie rakhis on each other's hands as a mark of unity.
2. This movement was connected with the Rowlatt Act of 1919.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: In 1905, Rabindranath Tagore encouraged Hindus and Muslims to tie rakhis on each other's hands as a mark of unity.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The rakhi movement was linked with the Partition of Bengal (1905), not the Rowlatt Act of 1919.

questions.question: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vande Mataram Movement.
The Swadeshi Movement started in August 1905 from Calcutta Town Hall against Lord Curzon's decision to partition Bengal. In Andhra Pradesh, it was called the Vande Mataram Movement. Leaders of the movement included Lokmanya Tilak (Poona and Bombay), Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab), and Chidambaram Pillai (Madras).

questions.question: What is the official reason given by Britishers after partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Administrative Convenience.
The official reason given by the British for the partition of Bengal was administrative convenience. However, the real reason was to divide and weaken the growing nationalist movement in Bengal. After Partition, the Swadeshi movement gained even more momentum, and the British were forced to revoke the partition in 1911.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Before the Partition of Bengal in 1905, Bengal was the biggest province of British India, consisting of parts of Bihar and Orissa.
Reason (R): Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal in 1905 to separate the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
The Partition of Bengal was announced by Lord Curzon on 20th July 1905. Bengal was indeed the biggest province of British India before partition. The reorganization separated the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas, which explains why Bengal was partitioned.

questions.question: Which of the following parties supported the move for partition of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is All India Muslim League.
The All India Muslim League supported the move for the partition of Bengal. The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Aga Khan III, Khwaja Salimullah, Hakim Ajmal Khan, and Waqar-ul-Mulk.

questions.question: Moved by the Swadeshi Movement, ______ painted his famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Abanindranath Tagore.
Abanindranath Tagore painted his famous image of Bharat Mata portraying her as an ascetic figure in 1905. The painting depicts a saffron-clad divine woman holding a book, sheaves of paddy, a piece of white cloth, and a rosary in her four hands.

questions.question: Once the Time Magazine had mocked Gandhi's physical size but to whom did it compare his martyrdom later on?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Abraham Lincoln.
Time magazine in its earlier coverage had mocked Mahatma Gandhi's small physical stature. However, after his assassination on 30 January 1948, Time compared Gandhi's martyrdom to that of Abraham Lincoln, recognizing the magnitude of his sacrifice for peace and freedom. Like Lincoln, Gandhi was portrayed as a leader who gave his life for unity and justice in his nation.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was launched in Bardoli in 1917.
Reason (R): Pandit Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi to Champaran to study the grievances of indigo farmers.
questions.option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.option_3: A is true, but R is false
questions.option_4: A is false, but R is true
questions.solution:
The correct answer is A is false, but R is true.
  • Assertion (A) is false: Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India was launched in Champaran (1917), not Bardoli.
  • Reason (R) is true: Pandit Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi to Champaran to study the grievances of indigo farmers.
  • The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel for the farmers of Bardoli.

questions.question: Who was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March on 12 March 1930?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Irwin (1926-1931).
Other events during his tenure:
  • Simon Commission to India (1927)
  • Nehru Report (1928)
  • Deepavali Declaration (1929)
  • Lahore session of Congress (Purna Swaraj Resolution) 1929
  • First Round Table Conference (1930)
  • Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931)

questions.question: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1931.
The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, the Viceroy of India (1926-1931). The pact ended the Civil Disobedience Movement, initiated by Gandhi with the Salt March, and was signed before the Second Round Table Conference in London.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Round Table Conferences:
1. Mahatma Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference.
2. Mahatma Gandhi participated in all the three Round Table Conferences held in London.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Only 2.
Mahatma Gandhi went only to the Second Round Table Conference (1931). He did not attend the First (1930) or Third (1932) Round Table Conferences. Therefore, statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is incorrect.

questions.question: In which of the following places did Mahatma Gandhi, along with other Indians, establish the Natal Congress to fight against racial discrimination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is South Africa.
The Natal Indian Congress was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in 1894 to combat discrimination against Indians in South Africa. Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 and returned to India on 9 January 1915.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Dandi March was started by Mahatma Gandhi from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930.
2. The Quit India Movement was launched in 1930 alongside the Salt Satyagraha to strengthen the freedom struggle.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2 only.
  • Statement 1 is correct: The Dandi March was started by Mahatma Gandhi from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 5 April 1930.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The Quit India Movement was launched later in 1942, not in 1930.

questions.question: Which of the following leaders had gone to Lucknow to invite Mahatma Gandhi to see the plight of the peasants in Champaran?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Raj Kumar Shukla.
The local Congress leaders Brajkishore Prasad and Raj Kumar Shukla first met Mahatma Gandhi at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in 1916 and invited him to have first-hand experience of the plight of Champaran peasants. Gandhi arrived in Champaran on April 15, 1917.

questions.question:
Match the following Pacts with the year in which they were signed:
Column A (Pacts)Column B (Years)
1. Gandhi-Ambedkar Pact (Poona Pact)A. 1931
2. Gandhi-Irwin Pact B. 1932
3. Lucknow Pact C. 1916
4. Delhi Pact (Rajendra Prasad – Liaquat Ali Pact) D. 1947
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1–B, 2–A, 3–C, 4–D.
  • The Poona Pact (Gandhi-Ambedkar Pact) was signed in 1932 (B).
  • The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in 1931 (A).
  • The Lucknow Pact was signed in 1916 (C).
  • The Delhi Pact (Rajendra Prasad – Liaquat Ali Pact) was signed in 1947 (D).
